stories.title: China delivers a one-two punch to America’s AI dominance
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: Chinese AI leaders (Moonshot, Alibaba) are challenging US dominance in the AI field.
Their newly unveiled models claim competitive performance against OpenAI and Anthropic at lower costs.
The rapid development signals a tightening of the perceived lead for American AI companies.

stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under text-generation, indicating its primary function as a large language model.
The associated tags (transformers, safetensors, llama) confirm its relevance within the modern NLP/AI ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The model is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro' model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text-generation tasks, indicating its capability in generative AI applications.
Key associated technologies include transformers and safetensors, standard components in modern LLM deployment.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent tasks show up to 90% faster performance based on the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using its MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to faster response times and higher quality model outputs.
The updated engine also demonstrates improved memory efficiency when running models.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents can run entirely on the user's local hardware.
Integration with Ollama is built-in, leveraging local LLM execution capabilities.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance gains.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware for optimized execution.
The feature is currently available in a preview build, indicating ongoing development.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, emphasizing on-device processing for privacy and control.
The core value proposition is running AI tasks entirely on the user's own device rather than in the cloud.

stories.title: AliExpress fined almost $630 million over illegal product sales
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: AliExpress has been fined approximately €550 million (about $629 million) by the European Commission.
The fine stems from violations of the EU's Digital Services Act (DSA).
The core violation was the platform's failure to implement effective measures against the sale of illegal, unsafe, or counterfeit products.

stories.title: India's first privately-developed rocket reaches orbit on dramatic debut launch
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: India achieved a significant milestone with the successful orbital launch of its first privately developed rocket.
The launch marks a major step forward in the advancement of private space technology within India.
The success is highlighted by the sentiment of the involved personnel, indicating a breakthrough achievement.

stories.title: Google-backed satellites for wildfire detection launch as smoke chokes US, Canada
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Google-backed FireSat program is launching satellites specifically designed for wildfire detection.
The new system aims to identify wildfires that current satellite technology fails to detect.
The deployment is highly relevant given the current severe wildfire smoke impacting the US and Canada.

stories.title: CRAFT: Clustering Rubrics to Diagnose Weak LLM Capabilities and Generate Targeted Fine-Tuning Data
stories.author: Yunzhong He
bullet_points: Introduces CRAFT, a new method to move beyond simple performance measurement in LLM evaluations.
CRAFT diagnoses the underlying *reason* for LLM failures by converting rubric-based evaluation datasets into specific capability weaknesses.
The tool facilitates the generation of targeted fine-tuning data, directly informing the next iteration of model improvement.

stories.title: Harmonizing AI Safety Thresholds
stories.author: Markov Grey
bullet_points: Frontier AI companies use disparate capability thresholds, hindering third-party verification and cross-company comparison.
Lack of common minimum safety thresholds risks inconsistent risk mitigation and a 'race to the bottom' in safety standards.
The paper proposes a methodology to derive harmonized safety thresholds across three distinct risk domains (including misuse risks).

stories.title: PagedWeight: Efficient MoE LLM Serving with Dynamic Quality-Aware Weight Quantization
stories.author: Sasa Misailovic
bullet_points: Introduces PagedWeight, a new method to improve the serving efficiency of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Large Language Models (LLMs).
Addresses the memory tension in MoE serving between large model weights and growing KV caches.
Achieves efficiency by dynamically quantizing MoE model weights at runtime, balancing weight precision against KV cache size.

stories.title: Learning Standard Model structure from LHC data with Riemannian flow matching
stories.author: Oleg Ruchayskiy
bullet_points: Introduces ShellFlow, a novel Riemannian conditional flow matching model.
The model uses a single transformer to learn the structure of the Standard Model from LHC data.
It successfully spans a massive range of invariant masses (sub-GeV to TeV), surpassing the coverage of single Monte Carlo samples.

stories.title: Frontier AI performance across the business disciplines: a case-grounded benchmark of knowledge work and analytical reasoning
stories.author: Mitch Weiss
bullet_points: Current LLM benchmarks fail to adequately measure real-world analytical knowledge work.
The research proposes a new case-grounded benchmark to test LLMs on complex white-collar tasks.
Key missing capabilities include synthesizing complex information and exercising judgment under uncertainty.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces improved performance and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to enhance model support across diverse hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically boosting capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of 'subagents' for complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added, enhancing the model's ability to access real-time information.

stories.title: Beyond grep: The case for a context-rich AI coding harness
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: The article discusses the need for 'context-rich AI coding harnesses' beyond simple tools like grep.
It features Vinay Perneti of Augment Code, focusing on the intersection of large language models and software development.
The core theme is improving AI assistance in coding by providing deeper contextual understanding to the models.

stories.title: Will AI fix prior authorization—or make it worse?
stories.author: Joshua Cohen, Undark Magazine
bullet_points: A government pilot program is testing the use of Artificial Intelligence in insurance coverage decisions.
The article explores the dual potential of AI: whether it can streamline or complicate the prior authorization process.
This touches upon the intersection of AI adoption, healthcare administration, and regulatory technology.

stories.title: Evaluating Open-Weight LLMs for Generating Structured Threat Information for Autonomous Vehicle Vulnerabilities
stories.author: Md Rayhanur Rahman
bullet_points: The research focuses on using Open-Weight Large Language Models (LLMs) to process cybersecurity data.
The specific application is transforming unstructured vulnerability data (like CVEs) into structured threat information.
The target domain is Connected and Autonomous Vehicles (CAVs), addressing critical security needs in this sector.

stories.title: When Does Muon Help Agentic Reinforcement Learning?
stories.author: Hao Sun
bullet_points: The paper investigates the utility of the Muon optimizer compared to AdamW in Reinforcement Learning (RL) post-training.
Applying Muon specifically to hidden weight matrices within the GiGPO framework significantly boosted validation success from 0.290 to 0.546.
The findings suggest Muon offers a substantial performance advantage in sparse-reward agentic RL tasks over standard AdamW controls.

stories.title: An Exam for Active Observers
stories.author: Willie Neiswanger
bullet_points: The paper addresses the concept of 'active observation' in human vision, where gaze is continuously guided by hypotheses rather than static snapshots.
It highlights a gap in current multimodal large language models (MLLMs) and vision-language benchmarks regarding whether they exhibit this active observational behavior.
The authors introduce 'ActiveVision,' a new benchmark designed to empirically measure active observation in ML systems.

stories.title: When Do Multi-Agent Systems Help? An Information Bottleneck Perspective
stories.author: Shuiwang Ji
bullet_points: The paper investigates when Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) outperform Single-Agent Systems (SAS) in complex tasks.
It introduces an Information Bottleneck perspective to analyze the performance differences between MAS and SAS.
A key finding is the difference in context handling: SAS uses a single shared context, while MAS uses isolated local contexts.

stories.title: ToolSciVer: Multimodal Scientific Claim Verification with Visual Tool Augmented Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Rui Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces ToolSciVer, a novel framework for Multimodal Scientific Claim Verification (MSCV).
Addresses limitations in existing methods, specifically struggling with locating decisive visual evidence and interpreting structured scientific visuals.
Employs a tool-augmented Reinforcement Learning approach to integrate multimodal observations for reliable scientific reasoning.

stories.title: A Methodology for Auditable Trustworthiness Levels in AI Lifecycle Governance
stories.author: Andrea Ferrario
bullet_points: Addresses the need for ongoing, auditable trustworthiness assessment throughout the AI lifecycle.
Identifies a gap where existing AI trustworthiness work is either too abstract or too narrowly focused.
Proposes a lightweight methodology to bridge the gap between technical metrics and governance requirements.

stories.title: Understanding Reasoning from Pretraining to Post-Training
stories.author: Pavel Izmailov
bullet_points: The paper addresses a gap in LLM research by linking pretraining choices to the effectiveness of Reinforcement Learning (RL) post-training.
It highlights two open questions: how pretraining parameters (size, data) affect RL returns, and the specific functional impact of RL on the model.
The study aims to overcome the challenges posed by the vast and uncontrolled nature of standard LLM pretraining corpora.

stories.title: Physics-enhanced reinforcement learning for real-time optimal control of dynamical systems
stories.author: Andrea Manzoni
bullet_points: The paper addresses the sample inefficiency of Reinforcement Learning (RL) when applied to complex dynamical systems.
It proposes using physics-enhanced RL to improve the real-time optimal control of these systems.
This approach aims to mitigate limitations caused by the curse of dimensionality in high-dimensional control problems.

stories.title: When Does Muon Help Agentic Reinforcement Learning?
stories.author: Hao Sun
bullet_points: The paper investigates the utility of the Muon optimizer in agentic Reinforcement Learning (RL) post-training, comparing it against AdamW.
Applying Muon specifically to hidden weight matrices within the Group-in-Group Policy Optimization (GiGPO) framework significantly improved validation success from 0.290 to 0.546.
The findings suggest Muon offers a substantial performance advantage in sparse-reward RL tasks over standard AdamW controls.

stories.title: An Exam for Active Observers
stories.author: Willie Neiswanger
bullet_points: The paper addresses the gap in current benchmarks regarding whether multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) perform 'active observation,' mimicking human vision.
Active observation, where gaze is continuously redirected by hypotheses, is posited as essential for human cognitive tasks.
The authors introduce 'ActiveVision,' a new benchmark designed to empirically measure the concept of active observation in ML models.

stories.title: PRISA: Proactive Infrastructure LiDAR Framework for Intersection Safety Assessment
stories.author: Hoang H. Nguyen
bullet_points: Introduces PRISA, a new LiDAR framework designed for proactive safety assessment at urban intersections.
Focuses on real-time, continuous monitoring to anticipate traffic conflicts involving vehicles and vulnerable road users (VRUs).
Utilizes privacy-preserving and low-light-robust roadside sensors for long-term traffic observation.

stories.title: An Exam for Active Observers
stories.author: Willie Neiswanger
bullet_points: The paper addresses the concept of 'active observation' in human vision, where gaze is continuously redirected based on hypotheses.
It posits that current multimodal large language models (MLLMs) may not exhibit this active observation, which is a key empirical question.
The authors introduce 'ActiveVision,' a new benchmark designed to empirically measure active observation in ML models.

stories.title: ToolSciVer: Multimodal Scientific Claim Verification with Visual Tool Augmented Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Rui Zhang
bullet_points: ToolSciVer is a novel framework designed for Multimodal Scientific Claim Verification (MSCV).
It addresses limitations in current methods by integrating visual evidence (figures, tables, charts) with textual context.
The framework utilizes tool-augmented Reinforcement Learning to accurately locate and reason over complex scientific visuals.

stories.title: Rate-Utility Frontiers for Language Encodings: Comparing Tokens, Bytes, and Pixels Under Controlled Linguistic Content
stories.author: Desmond Elliott
bullet_points: The research compares three different text encoding methods (tokens, bytes, and pixels) used in language models.
The study controls for linguistic content and downstream capacity across thirteen languages and five scripts.
It investigates what information each encoding preserves when subjected to a shared bottleneck.

stories.title: Understanding Reasoning from Pretraining to Post-Training
stories.author: Pavel Izmailov
bullet_points: The paper addresses the gap between LLM pretraining and subsequent Reinforcement Learning (RL) fine-tuning.
It seeks to answer how pretraining choices (like model size and data) influence the effectiveness of RL compute.
The research aims to elucidate the specific mechanisms by which RL modifies the model's capabilities.

stories.title: Frontier Language Models Struggle to Copy: Text Can Be Better Viewed in 2D
stories.author: Kaifeng Lyu
bullet_points: Frontier Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit a surprising failure in a basic task: exactly copying input strings.
The research attributes this failure to the limitations of positional encodings within Transformer architectures.
The models' inductive bias favors local context matching shortcuts over precise positional retrieval.

stories.title: Loop the Loopies!
stories.author: Bryan Dai
bullet_points: Introduction of 'Loopie,' a new family of powerful looped Transformer models.
The models utilize a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture, with sizes including 20B and 6B parameters.
Loopie specifically addresses a known limitation in looped Transformers regarding scaling compute versus increasing parameter count.

stories.title: Exploit brokers pay $500k for WordPress RCEs. I found one with GPT5.6 and $25
stories.author: infosecau
bullet_points: Exploit brokers are reportedly paying high sums ($500k) for Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerabilities in WordPress.
The author claims to have discovered a WordPress RCE vulnerability using GPT-5.6.
The author suggests their discovered exploit is available for a low price ($25).

stories.title: The EU is about to sell our most sensitive data to the US for visa-free travel
stories.author: rapnie
bullet_points: The EU plans to share sensitive personal data with the US.
The data sharing is intended to facilitate visa-free travel for EU citizens to the US.
The news originates from Hacker News, suggesting a focus on privacy and geopolitical tech implications.

stories.title: Moonshine: Lets you stream games from your PC to any device running Moonlight
stories.author: wertyk
bullet_points: Moonshine is a new tool designed for game streaming.
It allows users to stream games from a PC to various devices.
It utilizes Moonlight technology for the streaming functionality.

stories.title: Streaming LLM responses in TypeScript: SSE, ReadableStream, and the React 19 useChat hook.
stories.author: thegdsks
bullet_points: Focuses on a practical implementation detail: streaming Large Language Model (LLM) responses.
Covers specific web technologies like Server-Sent Events (SSE) and ReadableStream for efficient data transfer.
Highlights integration with modern frontend frameworks, specifically mentioning the React 19 useChat hook.

stories.title: 'Local' Solves Where Your Data Goes. It Doesn't Solve What Your Agent Does
stories.author: p0rt
bullet_points: Running AI agents locally addresses data sovereignty concerns but does not inherently solve all security risks.
Security vulnerabilities like prompt injection, provenance failures, and privilege escalation persist even when agents are run on local hardware.
The article advises on specific scenarios where local deployment is genuinely safe versus where 'local' is merely a marketing term.

stories.title: AI And Code Ownership: Who Is Responsible For Generated Code?
stories.author: nazar-boyko
bullet_points: The article addresses the complex legal question of code ownership when AI generates software.
It highlights the ambiguity surrounding intellectual property rights for AI-generated code.
This topic represents an important, evolving discussion within the software development and legal tech sectors.
